- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to match downward pressure.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak if sentiment remains bullish.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in long-term (30d) horizons; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 7–14d mean is below 30d average.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in second half of forecast window.
- In high volatility periods (e.g., 30d range > 5% from mean), model overfits short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
